headline: Official Shuttle and Parking Checks for Point Reyes Coastal Access
reservation: Backcountry camping and certain group activities require permits. The former winter shuttle to the Lighthouse and Chimney Rock has been indefinitely suspended; plan private-vehicle access subject to current road conditions, parking availability, and closures.

days.title: Headlands, Marine Life, and Maritime History
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from Point Reyes Station

stops.name: Point Reyes Lighthouse
stops.detail: Descend the historic stairs to the 1870s light station for expansive Pacific views and seasonal whale watching.

stops.name: Elephant Seal Overlook
stops.detail: Observe the resident colony of massive marine mammals from a safe distance near the Chimney Rock trailhead.

stops.name: Cypress Tree Tunnel
stops.detail: Walk through the interlocking Monterey cypress canopy leading to the historic maritime radio station.

days.driving: Allow 90 minutes total; narrow, winding roads require cautious speeds.
days.note: Fog can significantly reduce visibility on Sir Francis Drake Boulevard at any time.

days.title: Coastal Bluffs and Tule Elk Wilderness

stops.name: Tomales Point Trail
stops.detail: Hike through the Tule Elk Preserve to see herds grazing against the backdrop of Bodega Bay.

stops.name: Pierce Point Ranch
stops.detail: Explore the well-preserved 19th-century dairy complex that highlights the region's agricultural heritage.

days.driving: Allow 60 minutes; the northern peninsula involves paved but rural stretches.
days.note: Bring water as the Tomales Point area is exposed with no shade or potable sources.

days.title: Tidefalls and Fault Lines

stops.name: Alamere Falls
stops.detail: Trek to the rare coastal tidefall where freshwater drops directly onto the beach sands.

stops.name: Earthquake Trail
stops.detail: View the 1906 San Andreas Fault displacement at the Bear Valley Visitor Center interpretive walk.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes to trailheads; parking at Palomarin is limited and fills quickly.
days.note: The Alamere Falls hike is a strenuous 13-mile round trip; monitor tide levels for beach safety.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Lots at Palomarin and Bear Valley often reach capacity on weekends; have a secondary destination in mind. Use the designated overflow areas only if permitted by local signage.

intel.title: Connectivity Gaps
intel.text: Cellular service is non-existent in most western valley and coastal areas. Download all navigation maps and digital permits before leaving Point Reyes Station.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: Point Reyes Station and Olema serve as the final locations for fuel and groceries. No gasoline or prepared food services exist within the Seashore boundaries.

intel.title: Seasonal Transit
intel.text: Winter whale-watching months often trigger road closures to private vehicles at the South Beach junction. Check for the Sir Francis Drake shuttle operation dates usually starting in late December.

intel.title: Coastal Weather
intel.text: Temperatures can drop sharply when the marine layer moves in, regardless of inland heat. Layered clothing is essential for the variable conditions at the Lighthouse cliffs.

plan.arrival: Collect rental at STS, then stock up on local provisions in Point Reyes Station before heading to park visitor centers for orientation.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for main roads; check rental contracts for restrictions on unpaved trailhead access.
plan.goldenHour: Mount Wittenberg for sunset, though cloud cover often dictates visibility.
